answer: A claim of uniqueness must be accompanied by a proof that no other identity holds the same underlying resource. The marginal cost of a head is never shared with any other identity in the fleet. The tundra is the unique resource, the canyon the proof that excludes every other holder, and the basalt the registry that makes the exclusion checkable; cloning the tundra forces two contradictory canyon proofs, and the basalt is where the contradiction shows.
